records.name: Idempotency Key or Deterministic Operation
records.definition: The requirement that an operation carry a deduplication key or be deterministic so repeating it is safe.

records.name: Non-Repeatable Side Effects
records.definition: Side effects whose repetition changes the outcome, so retrying an operation double-applies them.

records.name: Safe Retries
records.definition: The ability to retry an operation without fear of duplicating its effects.

records.name: State Tracking
records.definition: The degree to which making operations idempotent requires tracking processed keys or prior state.

records.name: All-or-Nothing State Change
records.definition: The ability to apply a set of changes so that either all of them take effect or none do.

records.name: Distributed Scalability
records.definition: The degree to which enforcing atomic transactions across nodes limits how far a system can scale out.

records.name: Partial Commit
records.definition: Committing only some of a multi-step change after a failure, leaving state half-updated and inconsistent.

records.name: BASE/Eventual Consistency
records.definition: A consistency model favoring availability and soft state, letting replicas converge over time rather than staying strongly consistent.

records.name: Distributed Availability
records.definition: The degree to which insisting on strong transactional consistency reduces availability across a distributed system.

records.name: Durability
records.definition: The degree to which committed data survives crashes and is never lost once acknowledged.

records.name: Strong Transactional Guarantees
records.definition: The ability to guarantee that a group of operations is atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable.

records.name: Consistency Rules
records.definition: The requirement that the invariants a transaction must preserve be defined for its scope.

records.name: Hidden Distributed Transaction
records.definition: A transaction that silently spans service boundaries, coupling systems that should commit independently.

records.name: Large Transaction Scope
records.definition: The degree to which widening a transaction to cover more work increases contention and failure surface.

records.name: Safe State Mutation
records.definition: The ability to mutate state within a bounded transaction so partial failures cannot corrupt it.

records.name: Coordinated Persistence
records.definition: The ability to commit a set of related changes together as one atomic unit of work.

records.name: Repository Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which coordinating saves through a unit of work adds indirection to the persistence layer.

records.name: Scattered Save Calls
records.definition: Persisting related changes through many independent save calls, so a mid-sequence failure leaves partial state.

records.name: Inconsistent Replicas/Models
records.definition: Replicas or models that disagree on the same data, so reads return conflicting answers.

records.name: Reliable State
records.definition: The ability to trust that stored state always satisfies its invariants.

records.name: Dirty Reads/Writes
records.definition: Reading or overwriting another transaction's uncommitted changes, so a rollback leaves corrupt data.

records.name: Safe Concurrent Operations
records.definition: The ability to run concurrent transactions without their intermediate states interfering.

records.name: Safe Parallel Mutation
records.definition: The ability to let multiple actors mutate shared state in parallel without corrupting it.

records.name: Shared State Identification
records.definition: The requirement that all state shared between concurrent actors be identified before it is guarded.

records.name: Blind Overwrite
records.definition: Writing over another actor's update without checking whether the data changed first, silently losing it.

records.name: Conflict Detection
records.definition: The ability to detect that data changed since it was read, so a conflicting write can be rejected.

records.name: Retry Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which rejecting conflicting writes pushes retry-and-merge logic onto callers.

records.name: Version Field
records.definition: A field on a record whose value changes on each write, used to detect concurrent modification.

records.name: Lock Ownership
records.definition: The requirement that a lock be exclusively held by one actor for the duration of a critical section.

records.name: Lock-Free Throughput
records.definition: The degree to which a design sustains high throughput by coordinating concurrent access without holding locks.

records.name: Strong Conflict Prevention
records.definition: The ability to prevent conflicting updates by locking data before it is modified.

records.name: Data Sharing
records.definition: The degree to which strictly isolating state limits components from directly sharing data.

records.name: Effect Boundaries
records.definition: The requirement that side effects be confined to explicit boundaries rather than scattered through pure logic.

records.name: Performance Optimization
records.definition: The degree to which pushing side effects to the edges can forgo in-place optimizations that mutate for speed.

records.name: Pure Core / Imperative Shell
records.definition: An arrangement that keeps decision logic pure and pushes all side effects to a thin outer shell.

records.name: Ad-Hoc Lock Ordering
records.definition: Ordering lock acquisition by hand-reasoning rather than a proven scheme, inviting deadlock.

records.name: Concurrency Correctness

distinctFrom.reason: Concurrency correctness is concurrent flows producing correct results, while deadlock freedom is those flows never halting for good.

records.definition: The degree to which concurrent flows produce correct results free of races and lost updates, for example because each unit's state is isolated.

records.name: Concurrent-Flow Modeling

distinctFrom.reason: Concurrent-flow modeling builds the explicit model of token flow, while reachability analysis examines which states that model can reach.

records.definition: The ability to model concurrent token flow explicitly so its behavior can be analyzed.

records.name: Deadlock Freedom

distinctFrom.reason: Deadlock freedom is never halting for good, while lock-free throughput is sustaining speed by not holding locks at all.

records.definition: The degree to which a concurrent design is provably free of states where progress halts permanently, which acquiring several locks pessimistically puts at risk.

records.name: Modeling Overhead
records.definition: The degree to which formally modeling concurrency as a net adds effort over writing the code directly.

records.name: Places and Transitions
records.definition: The requirement that a modeled system be expressed as places holding tokens and transitions that move them.

records.name: Reachability and Deadlock Analysis
records.definition: The ability to analyze which states a concurrent model can reach and whether any of them deadlock.

records.name: Reconciliation Job
records.definition: A technique for periodically comparing two copies of related state and repairing the differences found.

records.name: Merge Policy
records.definition: A technique for declaring how two concurrent changes to one value are combined.

records.name: Transaction Isolation Level
records.definition: A technique for choosing how much concurrent transactions see of each other's uncommitted and recent writes.

records.name: Make Immutable
records.definition: A technique for replacing in-place mutation with new values, so state shared between readers cannot change under them.

records.name: Read From Primary After Write
records.definition: A technique for routing a client's reads to the primary for a short time after it writes, so it sees its own write.

records.name: Consistency Contract
records.definition: A technique for stating which reads may be stale, for how long, and how a client learns that its write is visible.

records.name: Fix the Race
records.definition: A technique for removing a race by ordering, locking or making the shared state immutable, instead of retrying the test.

records.name: Apply Concurrency Control
records.definition: A technique for coordinating concurrent writers with locks, versions or ownership, so no write is lost.

records.name: Introduce Transaction Boundary
records.definition: A technique for declaring which writes commit or fail together.
